title: Find Longest Self-Contained Substring
summary: Determine the length of the longest substring within a given string that does not appear elsewhere in the string.
statement: Determine the length of the longest substring within a given string that does not appear elsewhere in the string. If no such substring exists, return -1.
constraints: s is a nonempty lowercase string.
A self-contained substring is proper (not the whole string) and contains every occurrence in s of each character it includes.
Return the greatest possible length, or -1 if no proper self-contained substring exists.
hints: A valid interval must begin at a character’s first occurrence and expand through the last occurrence of every character encountered.
Try each distinct first occurrence; reject if an encountered character begins earlier, otherwise extend the required right boundary.
Scan from left, update farthest=max(last[char]); whenever index=farthest record the proper interval length.
Expansion includes all later occurrences, the earlier-occurrence check includes all prior ones, and each possible valid left boundary is tested.
editorial: Expansion includes all later occurrences, the earlier-occurrence check includes all prior ones, and each possible valid left boundary is tested.
